channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Should Attract High-Spending Tourists, Says Former Official
item.description: Kazakhstan should focus on attracting wealthy tourists who spend $300-400 daily, rather than mass tourism, according to former Vice Minister of Tourism and Sports, Yerzhan Erkinbayev. He believes attracting a stable number of high-spending visitors is more beneficial than a large influx of budget travelers.

item.title: Woman Reports Kyrgyz Citizen Defrauding Compatriots in Russia to President
item.description: A resident of Kyrgyzstan's Jalal-Abad region has appealed to President Sadyr Japarov regarding a Kyrgyz citizen allegedly defrauding around 50-60 compatriots working in Russia. The total alleged damages exceed $100 million, with the woman claiming the suspect owes her $15 million. The president has instructed the Interior Ministry to investigate.

item.title: Freedom AI and Schneider Electric Partner to Develop Data Centers in Kazakhstan
item.description: Freedom AI and Schneider Electric have signed a memorandum of cooperation to develop modern data centers in Kazakhstan. The partnership aims to implement advanced engineering solutions for AI and high-performance computing projects, supporting Kazakhstan's goal of becoming a regional technology hub. Initial phases are planned for 2027-2028.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Dollar Exchange Rate Decreases for Fifth Consecutive Day
item.description: The dollar exchange rate in Uzbekistan has fallen for the fifth consecutive day. The Central Bank of Uzbekistan announced the official exchange rates for foreign currencies against the Uzbek soum, effective October 24. This marks a continued trend of depreciation for the US dollar.

item.title: Sadyr Japarov Suggested to Hold People's Kurultai Every Four Years
item.description: During a meeting with residents, a citizen proposed to Sadyr Japarov that the People's Kurultai be held every four years instead of annually, citing costs. President Japarov acknowledged the suggestion, stating that the frequency could be adjusted in the future.

item.title: Global Internet Under Threat: Millions of Hacking Attempts Detected After PHP Vulnerabilities Found
item.description: The global internet is facing a significant threat following the discovery of critical vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language, used by numerous websites and online services. Millions of hacking attempts have been recorded worldwide, prompting some banks and airlines to temporarily disable their sites.

item.title: President Tokayev Awards Cultural and Media Figures Ahead of Republic Day
item.description: In Astana, 62 figures from culture, arts, literature, and media received state awards from President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev ahead of Republic Day. The ceremony, led by Minister of Culture Arman Kyryqbayev, honored representatives from leading cultural institutions and media outlets, including Astana Opera and Qazaqstan TV.

item.title: Turkmen Citizen Dies in Severe Flooding in Istanbul
item.description: A Turkmen citizen has died in severe floods that hit Istanbul following heavy rainfall. The body of the 30-year-old, identified as Myrat Babajanov, was found in the Golden Horn. This brings the total death toll from the floods to five, with two others still missing. The floods caused significant damage to numerous buildings and vehicles.

item.title: American Investor Plans to Expand Vegetable Processing Plant in Kashkadarya
item.description: Wosune International plans to increase its investment in fruit and vegetable processing in Uzbekistan's Kashkadarya region to $50 million. The company, which has already invested $8.5 million, aims to produce high-quality dehydrated products for international markets, including major companies like Nestlé and Mars. The expanded facility will create 150 jobs.

item.title: Kazakh Women Share Experiences of Sexual Violence Under #IAmJaneDoe Campaign
item.description: Women in Kazakhstan are participating in the #IAmJaneDoe social media campaign, sharing personal accounts of sexual violence experienced during childhood and adolescence. Many survivors cited fear of judgment and distrust in law enforcement as reasons for their silence. The campaign aims to raise awareness and encourage reporting of such incidents.

item.title: Kazakhstan Government Rejects Moratorium on Fines for Retail Markups
item.description: The Kazakhstan government has not supported a moratorium on fines for retail markups in small neighborhood stores. Deputy Prime Minister Serik Zhumangarin stated that exceptions would create unequal market conditions. The current regulation limits markups on socially significant products to 15%.

item.title: Kazakhstan: New Chemical Production Facility Planned in Aktobe Region
item.description: A new production facility, valued at over 100 billion tenge, is planned for construction in the Aktobe region of Kazakhstan. The plant will produce ethylenamines on a 13.08-hectare site within the 'Aktobe' industrial zone. The project faces challenges due to high infrastructure and energy costs, but technology providers are ready to supply necessary information.

item.title: Global Report: Fathers in 66 Countries Lack Paid Paternity Leave
item.description: A report by UN Women and the World Bank highlights significant inequality in paid parental leave globally. In 66 countries, fathers are not guaranteed paid paternity leave, impacting gender equality and family responsibilities. The report notes that mothers often receive much longer paid leave, contributing to women's burden and limiting opportunities for families and economies.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Only 18% Pass State Language Exam on First Attempt
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan, only 18% of participants are passing the state language exam on their first try. Even potential presidential candidates Omurbek Suvanaliyev and Siymik Japiqayev failed to score enough points on the Kyrgyz language test. Japiqayev retook the test.

item.title: Nepal Seeks UN Aid to Cover Flood Damage Costs
item.description: Nepal will receive $20 million from the UN's Loss and Damage Fund to address the aftermath of devastating floods in August. This amount, however, represents less than 1% of the estimated $4.7 billion needed for recovery. The Prime Minister called the floods a warning about climate change.

item.title: Unwanted Pregnancies Put Turkmen Women in Dangerous Situations
item.description: Women in Turkmenistan have limited options for terminating unwanted pregnancies, with the law allowing only five weeks. Those who discover their pregnancy later must give birth or seek illegal, dangerous methods. Doctors warn of severe health risks and fatalities due to clandestine abortions, which have become a lucrative underground trade.

item.title: Uzbekistan Exceeds Cotton Harvest Target Amidst Persistent Irrigation Water Losses
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Agriculture announced the cotton harvest reached 4.63 million tons by October 22, surpassing its target by 3%. Mechanization accounted for 76% of the harvest. However, a recent study highlighted significant water losses in the country's irrigation systems, with an estimated 37% of water lost during transportation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Approves Drone Market Development Plan Until 2029
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has approved Kazakhstan's development plan for unmanned systems for 2026-2029. The plan outlines key directions for the implementation, production, and regulation of drone technologies. Responsible government bodies must report on progress twice annually to the Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Inaugurates Snow Leopard Research and Rehabilitation Center
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has opened the Ak Ilbirs snow leopard research and rehabilitation center in the village of Ananyevo, Issyk-Kul. The center aims to study snow leopard behavior and boost conservation efforts. The opening coincided with International Snow Leopard Day, with support from Russia's Republic of Tatarstan.

item.title: Three Companies Plan to Launch Driverless Taxi Service in Kazakhstan
item.description: inDrive, Pony.ai, and NVIDIA have signed an agreement to launch a driverless taxi service in Kazakhstan, with Astana potentially being the first test city. The collaboration will assess technical, commercial, and legal conditions for autonomous vehicles.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans Industrial Project with 1.5 Billion Som Funding
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to allocate 1.5 billion soms from the state budget to establish and develop industrial parks. The first site in Novopokrovka, Chuy region, will be developed with necessary infrastructure. A management company will be created to oversee these parks.

item.title: International Puppet Festival Unites Global Masters in Almaty
item.description: Almaty is hosting the IV International "Almaty Puppet Festival – 2026," gathering over 150 puppet art masters. The festival fosters professional exchange and strengthens international creative ties, showcasing national cultures and contemporary puppet theater trends.

item.title: HIMOYA Exhibition Explores Women's Memory and Protective Amulets
item.description: The HIMOYA exhibition at Almaty's Tselinny Center showcases Central Asian artists exploring inherited beliefs and women's experiences in preserving cultural identity. Works include protective amulets and themes of maternal memory, rituals, and protection.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China to Trial Driverless Trucks for Cross-Border Freight
item.description: Kazakhstan and China are planning to test driverless trucks on international routes for freight transport. An agreement was signed to develop trials and establish a joint center for autonomous transport, aiming to adapt Chinese technology to Kazakhstan's roads and requirements.

item.title: Georgian Parliament Speaker to Pay Official Visit to Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The Speaker of the Georgian Parliament, Shalva Papuashvili, will undertake an official visit to Kyrgyzstan. Preparations for the visit were discussed by the foreign ministers of both countries in Batumi on October 22. They also reviewed political, trade-economic, and transport-logistics ties, as well as cooperation in tourism, culture, and interregional contacts.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Infrastructure Fee for Industrial Park Residents
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering an infrastructure payment for companies in industrial parks, potentially up to 2% of annual turnover after production begins. The Ministry of Economy and Commerce drafted the proposal, which outlines new rules for industrial park creation and operation. Residents would contribute to maintaining and developing shared infrastructure.

item.title: New $8 Million Program to Protect Rare Wildlife in Central Asia's Mountains
item.description: A new five-year program, funded with up to $8 million primarily by the EU, will offer around 100 grants to local groups for wildlife conservation in the Pamir and Tien Shan mountains. Running from 2026 to 2031, the initiative coordinated by Fauna & Flora aims to protect threatened species and ecosystems across five Central Asian countries.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets Rosatom Director General on Nuclear Power Plant Project
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Alexey Likhachev, Director General of Rosatom, to discuss the construction of Uzbekistan's first integrated nuclear power plant. They reviewed progress on the first reactor building's foundation and design, and discussed training qualified personnel and developing infrastructure for a "nuclear city" near the plant.

item.title: Russian Academy of Sciences Representative Office to Open in Uzbekistan
item.description: A representative office of the Russian Academy of Sciences (RAS) is planned to open in Uzbekistan, affiliated with the Russian Trade Representation. This decision was made following a meeting between the Russian Trade Representative and the Vice-President of RAS. Similar offices will also be established in seven other countries to foster scientific partnerships.

item.title: First Central Asian NVIDIA AI Innovation Hub to Open in Dushanbe
item.description: The first AI Innovation Hub in Central Asia, supported by NVIDIA, is being established in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on the Area AI platform. The center aims to train AI specialists and implement Physical AI technologies in the country's industry. Its launch supports Tajikistan's national policy on AI development and UN resolutions on AI's role in sustainable development.

item.title: IMF Projects 1.3% Economic Contraction in Middle East and North Africa for 2026
item.description: The International Monetary Fund forecasts a 1.3% economic contraction across the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan, and Pakistan in 2026. This downward revision is attributed to the economic impact of the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran, disrupting energy, shipping, trade, and tourism. A recovery is possible in 2027 if the conflict eases and trade normalizes.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Health Ministry Addresses Concerns Over 'Stratus' COVID-19 Variant
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health has responded to reports of Russian tourists experiencing symptoms possibly linked to the 'Stratus' COVID-19 variant. The ministry stated that the epidemiological situation in the country is stable and the 'Stratus' variant has been present for some time, posing no threat to public health. They advised on preventive measures.

item.title: Astana power outage caused by aerial line failure, full restoration achieved
item.description: Astana experienced a temporary power outage on October 23rd due to a failure in the "Dostyk – Airport" aerial line. Several substations lost power for 17 minutes before full restoration. Specialists are investigating the exact cause of the malfunction. This incident follows a broader power disruption in Central Asia on August 14th, linked to issues at the Toktogul HPP.

item.title: Uzbekistan Increases Electricity Production
item.description: Uzbekistan is increasing its electricity generation capacity. This development is part of the country's efforts to meet growing energy demands and potentially enhance its energy sector's output. Further details on the specific measures or projects driving this increase are expected.

item.title: Jany Dostuk Village Thrives a Year After Kyrgyz-Tajik Border Demarcation
item.description: A year after the Kyrgyz-Tajik border demarcation agreement, the village of Jany Dostuk in Kyrgyzstan's Batken region has settled in. Established on land received in an 'hectare for hectare' exchange, the new village replaced the old Dostuk village, which was part of the 91 hectares ceded to Tajikistan. 181 families have relocated to the new settlement.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Stricter Penalties for Domestic Violence, Including Arrest
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering stricter penalties for domestic violence, including administrative arrest for physical abuse not constituting a criminal offense. The proposed bill also includes provisions for public works or short-term arrest for psychological and economic abuse. Police would gain the right to immediately confiscate weapons from alleged perpetrators without a court order.

item.title: Central Asian and Georgian Foreign Ministers Convene in Batumi for Diplomatic Talks
item.description: Foreign ministers from Central Asia and Georgia met in Batumi on October 23, 2026. The meeting, reported by Tajikistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, focused on strengthening political dialogue and expanding regional cooperation. Discussions also covered trade, economic, transport, communication, and cultural-humanitarian spheres, alongside international agenda issues.

item.title: Navoiy Region to Launch Glass Product Manufacturing Project with Chinese Company
item.description: A $76 million investment project for a glass container manufacturing plant is set to be implemented in Navoiy Region, Uzbekistan. The project, in collaboration with China's Qingdao Rongtai Glass Products, will utilize quartz raw materials. The plant aims for full production capacity within five years, with the first phase launching within a year.

item.title: UNICEF Urges Continued Efforts for Polio-Free Afghanistan
item.description: UNICEF Afghanistan emphasized the need for ongoing national efforts to eradicate polio and vaccinate all children, coinciding with World Polio Day. The organization highlighted the dedication of frontline workers. The warning comes as Afghanistan has recorded 42 cases of wild poliovirus type 1 this year, with six cases in neighboring Pakistan.

item.title: Uzbek President meets Rosatom head to discuss first nuclear power plant construction
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Rosatom Director General Aleksey Likhachev on October 23 to discuss the construction of Uzbekistan's first integrated nuclear power plant in Jizzakh region. Discussions included developing infrastructure, training personnel, and building a nuclear city near the plant. Construction of the first reactor building's foundation is ongoing.
